subject: dog chocolate
title: What If Your Dog Ate Your Chocolate?

scenes.text: What if your dog ate your chocolate? Nothing might happen for hours. That's the trap.
Chocolate contains theobromine, a cousin of caffeine. A dog's body needs about 17 hours to clear half of it.
Within about 2 to 12 hours, signs start: vomiting, thirst, restlessness. Bigger doses race the heart.
Darker means stronger. Baking chocolate packs nearly seven times more per gram than milk chocolate.
About 20 milligrams per kilo brings mild signs. Around 60 can cause seizures. Severe cases last up to 72 hours.
For a ten-kilo dog, one 100-gram dark bar comes close to seizure level. White chocolate barely registers.

description:
What if your dog ate your chocolate? Theobromine and caffeine in chocolate have a half-life of about 17.5 hours in dogs, versus a few hours in humans, and signs usually appear within hours (Merck Veterinary Manual, WSU).
Mild signs start around 20 mg/kg, seizures around 60 mg/kg; unsweetened baking chocolate holds about 15.5 mg/g against 2.3 mg/g in milk chocolate.
